stories.title: Baseline (as is)
stories.what_happened: Nothing has gone wrong yet. This is the plan for the coming year, before any disruption.
stories.what_the_plan_did: It serves 99.41% of demand at a landed cost of $21.76M, moving it in 2,684 truck trips. It is held for S&OP review rather than released automatically, because the supplied forecast and the statistical baseline disagree beyond tolerance in 1 planning period.

stories.title: A supplier goes dark
stories.what_happened: The flavour house that supplies Cola Flavour Concentrate shuts for 13 weeks, from day 7 to day 98.
stories.what_the_plan_did: It saw the shutdown coming and bought 7,911 L in the week before it (it would normally buy 400 L), bought 0 L while the vendor was shut, and carried on afterwards. Service held at 99.41%.

stories.title: A road closes
stories.what_happened: The road from Ashford Bottling to DC Alpha closes for two weeks, from day 7 to day 21.
stories.what_the_plan_did: It filled DC Alpha up before the road closed — 41 trucks in the first week, against 13 normally — sent 0 while it was shut, and rebuilt stock afterwards with 85 trucks in the following three weeks, against 71. Service held at 99.41%.

stories.title: A key account's promotion order
stories.what_happened: Ashford Grocers, the highest-priority account, places a promotion order for an extra 125k cases of Classic Cola, due on day 10.
stories.what_the_plan_did: Ashford Grocers were filled at 100.0%. The network absorbed it without anyone else going short.

assumptions: Vendor shut: day 7 to day 98 of the year.
Found out late: the baseline is kept until day 7, then re-planned as an emergency, the best re-plan possible.
Every plan is proven within ±$122,241 of the best possible; a difference inside that is not a finding.
Prices, costs and the rest of the year's demand are the baseline's.

takeaways.message: Acting ahead wins back $5.90M, 100% of the $5.87M hit.
takeaways.case: Found out on day 7, a supplier goes dark costs $5.87M of profit and service falls to 75.78%. Acting ahead wins back $5.90M, 100% of the $5.87M hit.
calc: Profit a year: baseline $27,078,962; found out on day 7 $21,204,228; acted ahead $27,106,083.
Hit of finding out late = baseline − found out late = $27,078,962 − $21,204,228 = $5,874,734.
Won back by acting ahead = acted ahead − found out late = $27,106,083 − $21,204,228 = $5,901,854.
Share won back = $5,901,854 ÷ $5,874,734 = 100.5%: the $27,121 over is inside the ±$122,241, so the page says all of it.
Read against the ±$122,241 the plans are proven to: a finding.
Orders served, by value: baseline 99.41%, found out late 75.78%, acted ahead 99.41%.
